title: The Fake Semester
premise: Tamsin Amberdale has survived two decades of foster homes and scholarship scrutiny by being invisible, so when the ghost of Ashcombe Academy starts leaving him handwritten notes in ink that shouldn't exist, he can't decide whether he's haunted or finally seen. The notes lead him to a hidden archive proving the school's founding family covered up a student's death a century ago — and that the same cover-up is protecting someone powerful today. As Tamsin assembles an unlikely crew of misfits to expose the truth before the winter arts showcase, he discovers the 'ghost' is a living student who faked her own disappearance, and that his beloved mentor is complicit in burying the past. In the end, Tamsin chooses public truth over private safety, testifying at the trustees' hearing and performing the audition under his real name — earning belonging not as a label, but as a choice.
about_author: Rosalind Reyes is a former boarding school librarian who spent years cataloguing marginalia left behind by generations of students. She writes stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Opening week at Ashcombe Academy: Tamsin catalogs his survival rules while scrubbing the boathouse for work-study. He finds a note addressed to him by name, written in ink that shifts color and won't smudge. Emotional beat: unease threaded with a dangerous thrill at being noticed.

chapters.title: The Rules of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing his foster-care history and why invisibility equals safety. His roommate Devi teases him into attending the welcome assembly where Headmaster Voss praises the school's 'impeccable record.' Beat: Tamsin's armor shown, and its first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A second note appears inside his locked locker, referencing something he said aloud only to himself. He researches the Ashcombe Ghost legend in the library and meets Juniper, a sharp-tongued archivist's assistant who knows too much about the legend. Beat: curiosity overtaking fear.

chapters.title: Juniper Knows Things
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Juniper. She reveals the ghost's notes have appeared every seven years, always to one student, always stopping abruptly. She warns Tamsin that the last recipient transferred out mid-year and never spoke again. Beat: alliance formed on shared suspicion.

chapters.title: The Audition Notice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Winter arts showcase auditions are announced; Tamsin's music scholarship requires participation, forcing him toward visibility he dreads. Mentor Mr. Calloway encourages him gently — almost knowingly. A third note names Calloway. Beat: dread that the ghost sees everything, including his soft spots.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sneaking into the restricted archive, they find a sealed 1904 file: a student, Wren Halloway, died during a showcase rehearsal, ruled accidental, records expunged. The ink on the old incident report matches the notes. Beat: the legend becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Crew of Misfits
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They recruit Devi (tech wizard), Theo (legacy kid with guilt), and Marisol (journalist expelled from the paper for asking questions). Five students, five reasons to want the truth. Beat: tentative belonging — the first group Tamsin hasn't had to perform for.

chapters.title: The Note That Lies
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A note arrives claiming Juniper is using him. Trust fractures; Marisol suspects forgery, testing handwriting against the archive documents. Someone else is writing notes now — or the ghost is lying. Beat: paranoia, first real conflict within the crew.

chapters.title: Wren Halloway's Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using his legacy access, Theo gets them into the sealed fourth-floor room where Wren lived. Behind a mirror: letters revealing Wren was silenced after discovering faculty embezzlement — a pattern, not an accident. Beat: grief for a stranger, fury at the institution.

chapters.title: Calloway's Warning
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Calloway privately urges Tamsin to drop it, promising to protect his scholarship. The kindness feels like a leash. Tamsin realizes his mentor may be both protector and prisoner of the school's secrets. Beat: betrayal's first sting; loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't a Ghost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following ink chemistry clues, they trap the note-writer: Wren Ashcombe-Halloway, a descendant who faked her own enrollment disappearance to investigate her ancestor's death from inside. She's been watching Tamsin because his file — his admissions essay — was flagged by Voss. Beat: revelation reframes everything; the haunting was a rescue mission.

chapters.title: Flagged
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Why would Voss flag a scholarship kid's essay? Digging in, they find Tamsin was admitted over a trustee's objection — and that the objection letter quotes Wren Halloway's confiscated diary, still held somewhere in Voss's office. Beat: Tamsin stops being an observer; this is his story now.

chapters.title: Devi's Long Night
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi builds a way to mirror Voss's office network during the showcase tech rehearsal. Mid-operation, security nearly catches them; Theo covers with a legacy-kid bluff that costs him his father's approval. Beat: sacrifice — belonging means paying for each other.

chapters.title: The Diary Pages
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Photographed diary pages reveal Wren Halloway knew she was being poisoned slowly and named her killer: a founder whose family still chairs the board — the same family Theo comes from. Beat: horror and heartbreak; Theo must choose blood or truth.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Confronted by his grandfather with evidence of the crew's snooping, Theo is offered early admission to any university he wants in exchange for naming names. He refuses. Beat: quiet heroism; the legacy kid burns the legacy.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Retaliation begins: Tamsin's work-study is revoked, Juniper is suspended, the archive is resealed, and Wren's cover identity is exposed — she'll be expelled within days. Beat: despair; justice outside the law looks like losing.

chapters.title: What We Do With Losing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals her endgame: she never needed to win quietly — she needed the truth undeniable before witnesses. The showcase, broadcast to alumni and trustees, is the stage. Beat: hope rebuilt as strategy; fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Reckoning
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The crew plans the double reveal: Marisol's exposé timed to the livestream, the diary projected during intermission, testimony from Calloway — whom Tamsin confronts and finally moves to conscience. Beat: resolve; Tamsin rehearses his song and his speech as one act.

chapters.title: Showcase
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The performance begins beautifully; then the lights flicker — Devi's signal — and the diary pages fill the screens. Voss tries to cut power; alumni murmur; the board chair storms out. Beat: controlled chaos, the point of no return.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Called before the emergency trustees' session, Tamsin speaks — not as a scholarship case number but as Tamsin Amberdale, naming what was done to Wren Halloway and what is done to kids like him. Calloway corroborates. Beat: climax; truth spoken plainly at last.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Fallout: Voss resigns, the archive opens, Wren is formally readmitted under her own name, and the Halloway scholarship is founded. Tamsin's future is uncertain but his is — no conditions, no labels. Beat: exhale; justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Epilogue in spring: Tamsin performs the piece he was once too afraid to attempt, dedicating it to 'everyone the record forgot.' The crew watches from the front row. Last line echoes the first note: you were seen all along. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
